title: The cosmic microwave background spectrum
caption: The CMB is the most perfect blackbody known, at T = 2.725 K. Wien's law puts its peak at λ = 2.898 mm K / 2.725 K = 1.06 mm, in the microwave band. It was emitted at about 3000 K and stretched by expansion (z ≈ 1100).
alt: Blackbody spectrum of the cosmic microwave background against wavelength in millimetres, peaking at 1.06 millimetres.
description: Planck curve for T = 2.725 K, scaled to peak at 1.
Shorter wavelengths fall off steeply; longer ones slowly (the Rayleigh–Jeans tail).
